reports.title: Heartflow Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Raises Full Year 2026 Guidance

guidance.heading: 2026 Annual Guidance
section: Ï | Total revenue of $262 million to $264 million (approximately 49% to 50% growth year-over-year), compared to previous guidance of $246 million to $250 million (approximately 40% to 42% growth year-over-year)
Ï | Non-GAAP gross margin of approximately 82.5%, compared to previous guidance of approximately 82%

desk.headline: Revenue up 57% to $72.9m, beat; 2026 revenue outlook raised again to $262–264m
results: Revenue rose 57% to $72.9m, well ahead of the $65.2m estimate; US sales grew 60% to $67.9m, the fastest US growth in 11 quarters.
Growth came mainly from more US cases for both its FFRCT heart-artery test and its newer Plaque Analysis product.
Gross margin jumped to 83.6% (non-GAAP 83.8%) from 76.5%, helped by higher volumes and automation in its production team.
Losses shrank: GAAP net loss fell to $11.5m ($0.13 a share) from $50.9m, which had included large non-cash charges; non-GAAP loss was $2.7m ($0.03 a share).
Cash, equivalents and investments stood at $253.0m at quarter end.

guidance.summary: Heartflow raised its 2026 outlook again: revenue of $262–264m (up about 49–50%), from $246–250m before, and non-GAAP gross margin of about 82.5%, from about 82%. On the call it lifted its Plaque Analysis revenue outlook and said a 2027 outlook will come with Q4 results.

points: Plaque Analysis brought in $11.8m in Q3; active Plaque accounts are expected to reach about 1,300 by year-end, and insurer coverage widened to about 82% of US lives.
Management called the core FFRCT test durable, with new accounts taking about a year to reach full use; it expects steady gains, not a sudden jump.
Plaque pricing should be about flat in Q4, with the next contracted price step-up in Q1 2027.
The CFO kept the target of cash-flow profitability by mid-2028 and expects better cost leverage and smaller losses in 2027.
Management said the Q4 outlook assumes normal holiday slowdown and is set conservatively, as earlier in the year.
